s: A company is migrating its development and production workloads to a new organization in AWS Organizations. The company has created a separate member account for development and a separate member account for production. Consolidated billing is linked to the management account. In the management account, a solutions architect needs to create an 1AM user that can stop or terminate resources in both member accounts. Which solution will meet this requirement?
o: Create an IAM user and a cross-account role in the management account. Configure the crossaccount role with least privilege access to the member accounts.

Create an IAM user in each member account. In the management account, create a cross-account role that has least privilege access. Grant the IAM users access to the cross-account role by using a trust policy.

Create an IAM user in the management account. In the member accounts, create an IAM group that has least privilege access. Add the IAM user from the management account to each IAM group in the member accounts.
Create an IAM user in the management account. In the member accounts, create cross-account roles that have least privilege access. Grant the IAM user access to the roles by using a trust policy.
e: Cross account role should be created in destination(member) account. The role has trust entity to master account.

w.y: The IAM user lives in the management account and must act in member accounts. The standard cross-account pattern is a least-privilege role in each member account whose trust policy allows that user (or the management account) to assume it.

o.A: A role in the management account cannot grant permissions inside other accounts.
o.B: The user must be in the management account, and roles must be in the accounts where resources live.
o.C: IAM groups cannot contain users from another account.
o.D: Correct: roles in each member account trusted by the management-account user give cross-account access.
